<meta>This page continues the transition from the discussion of "Fixed" questions to the "Departure" questions. It concludes the section on the movement of figures and introduces a significant technical process in geomancy called "Inkilav" (Reversal or Transformation), specifically explaining how to interpret the final figures of a geomantic reading.</meta>

<page-num>५८</page-num>
<header>[ The Supreme Secret of Ramala ]</header>

After determining the nature of the **Outgoing** <term>Kharij</term> <note>original: *khārij*; figures indicating movement away</note> figures and others, and having certain knowledge, the practitioner should speak to the inquirer about the various types of **Departure** <term>Nirgama</term> <note>questions regarding leaving, traveling, or loss</note>, explaining whether the results will be auspicious or inauspicious, and whether they will come through ease or through great effort. ॥ १७ ॥

In this way, after contemplating all questions regarding departures and similar matters before the inquirer, the inquiry achieves success <term>Prashna-siddhi</term> only when the practitioner’s <term>Rammal</term> <note>a practitioner of Ramala geomancy</note> state of mind is steady, and there is faith in the science of geomancy and the teacher, along with purity of heart. ॥ १८ ॥

-> Thus ends the method for Departures and related inquiries. ॥ <-

-> Now, the purpose of Reversal. <-

I shall now speak of the results arising from questions involving **Reversal** <term>Inkilav</term> <note>original: *inkilāv* (from Arabic *inqilab*); a technical process where figures are transformed or "flipped"</note>. If the figure **Congregation** <term>Jamaat</term> <note>original: *jamāt* (from Arabic *jama‘at*); the 16th figure, often indicating a group or conclusion</note> appears in the designated place, one should judge the results from its two roots <note>the figures in the 13th and 14th houses which "produce" the later figures</note>. ॥ १९ ॥

If the figures are **Outgoing** <term>Kharij</term> and are Auspicious, they grant success in questions of departure. If they are **Incoming** <term>Dakhil</term> <note>original: *dākhil*; figures indicating entry or return</note> and Auspicious, they grant success in questions of arrival. ॥ २० ॥

Similarly, if they are **Fixed** <term>Sabit</term> <note>original: *thābit*; figures indicating stability</note> and Auspicious, they grant success in stationary tasks. In **Middling** <term>Madhyama</term> figures, there is success if the figure is strong, and only slight success if the figure is weak. ॥ २१ ॥

Through **Reversal** <term>Viparyayana</term> <note>synonym for Inkilav; turning over or inversion</note>, success is not achieved; however, one should deliberate on all factors as before, regarding whether the signs are auspicious or otherwise. One should judge the entirety of the inquiry section as previously described. ॥ २२ ॥

Questions concerning **Items held in the fist** <term>Mushti</term>, **Silent questions** <term>Muka</term> <note>where the inquirer does not speak their question aloud</note>, or questions about letters and time-periods, are settled without the use of Reversal; therefore, Reversal should not be applied to them. ॥ २३ ॥

In this manner, the judgment for all houses has been stated in a general sense. Now, I shall describe the specific characteristics pertaining to each individual house. ॥ २४ ॥

**Commentary—** Now the purpose of **Reversal** <term>Inkilav</term> is explained: At the time of a question arising from Reversal, if the figure **Congregation** <term>Jamaat</term> appears in the 15th house, one should speak the result based on its "roots," which are the 13th and 14th houses. ॥ १९ ॥ It is like this: if the figures in the 13th and 14th houses are **Outgoing** <term>Kharij</term> and are Auspicious, they grant success to a question about departure. If they are **Incoming** <term>Dakhil</term> and Auspicious, they grant success to a question about arrival.

<summary>This page concludes the rules for interpreting "Departure" questions and introduces the "Inkilav" (Reversal) method, which uses the 13th and 14th houses as "roots" to provide a final answer when the figure "Jamaat" appears.</summary>
<keywords>Nirgama (Departure), Inkilav (Reversal), Rammal (Geomancer), Jamaat (Congregation), Kharij (Outgoing), Dakhil (Incoming), Sabit (Fixed), geomantic houses</keywords>

1 ‘Where stands yon sage, towards [facing] the sun’s orb, immovable as the trunk-of-a-tree, (his) body half-buried in an ant-hill, with (his) breast closely-encircled by a snake’s-skin, round the throat excessively pinched by a necklace (formed) of the tendril of a withered creeper, wearing a circular-mass-of-matted-hair enveloping (his) shoulders (and) filled with bird’s-nests.’ *Valmīkārdha*, &c., so read K. and the Mackenzie MS.; the other Deva-n., *valmīkāgra*. *Valmīka* (=*krimi-kṛita-mṛittikācaya*) is the mound of earth thrown up by the large ants of India. ->Mātali:<-

This is the very difference between Indra and a long-lived hero.

->King:<-

Mātali, in which region is the hermitage of Marīca?

->Mātali: || Pointing with his hand ||<-

**With a body half-buried in an ant-hill, his chest tightly encircled by a snake’s skin, excessively pinched at the throat by a necklace made of the tendril of a withered creeper, and wearing a massive circle of matted hair that covers his shoulders and is filled with birds' nests, there the sage stands, immovable as the trunk of a tree, facing the sun's orb.** <note>Verse 175. This describes the extreme penance of an ascetic.</note>

<note>A cloud of dust is seen rising in advance of us; the chariot of thee reining in thy steeds, although it has descended to the earth, is not observed to have done so because of its not touching the surface of the ground. The commentator K. equates <term>upodha-śabdāḥ</term> <gloss>those with sound arrived</gloss> to <term>prāpta-dhvanayaḥ</term> <gloss>those having reached a state of making sound</gloss>. Mātali remarks on the difference between the chariot of Indra and that of mortal heroes. Where stands yon sage, facing the sun’s orb, immovable as the trunk of a tree, his body half-buried in an ant-hill, his breast closely encircled by a snake’s skin, his throat excessively pinched by a necklace formed of the tendril of a withered creeper, wearing a circular mass of matted hair enveloping his shoulders and filled with birds' nests. <term>Valmīka</term> <gloss>the mound of earth thrown up by large ants</gloss> is the mound. These hillocks sometimes rise to the height of eight or ten feet in Bengal and are held sacred. Such was the immovable impassiveness of this ascetic that the ants had thrown up their mound as high as his waist without being disturbed, and the birds had built their nests in his hair. The serpent’s skin was used by the ascetic in place of the regular Brahmanical cord, called <term>yajñopavīta</term> <gloss>sacred thread</gloss>.</note>

<summary>Mātali identifies the hermitage of Marīca, describing the ascetic in a state of extreme penance, and distinguishes the nature of divine travel from mortal movement.</summary>

मिन्द्रियद्वारा वा स्वतो वा विषयस्य संस्क्रियाऽभिव्यक्तिस्तस्याः कारणं यथा रूपस्याऽऽलोकः । विकारकारणं मनसो विषयान्तरम् । यथा हि कण्डोः समाहितमनसो वल्लकीविपञ्च्यमानपञ्चमस्वरश्रवणसमनन्तरमुन्मीलिताक्षस्य <gloss>१</gloss> स्वरूपलावण्ययौवनसंपन्नामप्सरसं प्रम्लोचामीक्षमाणस्य समाधिमपहाय तस्यां सक्तं मनो बभूवेति । अत्रैव निदर्शनमाह—यथाऽग्निः पाक्यस्य <gloss>२</gloss> तण्डुलादेः कठिनायवयवसंनिवेशस्य प्रशिथिलावयवसंयोगलक्षणस्य विकारस्य कारणम् । सत एव विषयस्य प्रत्ययकारणं धूमज्ञानमग्निज्ञानस्येति । ज्ञायत इति ज्ञानमग्निश्चासौ ज्ञानं चेत्यग्निज्ञानं तस्य । एतदुक्तं भवति—वर्तमानस्यैवाग्नेर्ज्ञेयस्य प्रत्ययकारणतया कारणमिति । औत्सर्गिकी निरपेक्षाणां कारणानां कार्यक्रिया प्राप्तिस्तस्याः कुतश्चिदपवादोऽप्राप्तिः । यथा निम्नोपसर्पणस्वभावानामपां प्रतिबन्धः सेतुना तथैहापि बुद्धिसत्त्वस्य सुखप्रकाशशीलस्य स्वाभाविकी सुखविवेकख्यातिजनकता प्राप्तिः । सा कुतश्चिद्धर्मात्तमसो वा प्रतिबन्धान्न भवति । धर्माद्योगाङ्गानुष्ठानाद्वा तदपनये तदप्रतिबद्धवृत्तिस्वभावत एव तज्जनकता तदाप्नोति । यथा वक्ष्यति—निमित्तमप्रयोजकं प्रकृतीनां वरणभेदस्तु ततः क्षेत्रिकवदिति ।

तदेवं विवेकख्यातिलक्षणकार्यापेक्षया प्राप्तिकारणमुक्तम् । अवान्तरकार्यापेक्षया तु तदेव वियोगकारणमित्याह—वियोगकारणमिति । अन्यत्वकारणमाह—अन्यत्वकारणं यथा सुवर्णकारः सुवर्णस्य, कटककुण्डलकेयूरादिभ्यो भिन्नाभिन्नस्य भेदविवक्षया कटकादिभिन्नस्याभेदविवक्षया कटकाद्यभिन्नस्य सुवर्णस्य कुण्डलादन्यत्वम् । तथा च कटककारी सुवर्णकारः कुण्डलादभिन्नसुवर्णादन्यत्कुर्वन्नन्यत्वकारणम् । अग्निरपि पाक्यस्यान्यत्वकारणं यद्यपि तथाऽपि धर्मिणो धर्मयोः पुलाकत्वतण्डुलत्वयोर्भेदाविवक्षया धर्मयोरुपजनापायेऽपि धर्म्यनुवर्तत इति न तस्यान्यत्वं शक्यं वक्तुमिति विकारमात्रकारणत्वमुक्तमिति न संकरः । न च संस्थानभेदो धर्मिणोऽन्यत्वकारणमिति व्याख्येयम् । सुवर्णकार इत्यस्यासंगतेः । बाह्यमन्यत्वकारणमुपन्यस्याऽऽध्यात्मिकमुदाहरति—एवमेकस्येति । अविद्या कमनीयेयं कन्यकेत्यादिज्ञानम् <gloss>४</gloss> । तन्मोहयोगात्त एव स्त्रीप्रत्ययो

<header>Vyāsa Bhāṣya with Vācaspati’s Commentary [2 Sādhanapāda</header>

...just as light is for form, so is form-knowledge; the cause of change of the mind is a different object. Just as fire is for what is to be cooked. The cause of cognition is the knowledge of smoke for the knowledge of fire. The cause of attainment is the practice of the limbs of Yoga. The cause of separation is the same, regarding impurity. The cause of distinctness is, for example, the goldsmith for gold. Thus, in the case of one perception of a woman, the root is ignorance (<term>avidyā</term>) in the state of delusion, aversion in the state of being painful...

<column-break/>

...or through the senses, or by itself, the refinement of the object is manifestation; its cause is, for example, light for form. The cause of change of the mind is a different object. For example, when a mind that was concentrated on a woman <note>original: "kandor samāhitamanaso..."</note> suddenly hears the fifth note played on a lute, the eyes open, and seeing a celestial maiden possessing the beauty of form and youth, it abandons the samādhi and becomes attached to her. Here, it gives a demonstration: **"Just as fire is for what is to be cooked,"** like rice, which is the cause of the change—the softening of the conjunction of parts of something previously hard. For something that already exists, the cause of cognition is the knowledge of smoke for the knowledge of fire. "Knowledge" is that which is known, and "fire" is the knowledge; it is the knowledge of fire. This is what is meant: for the existing fire that is to be known, it is the cause of the cognition. The acquisition of the work of causes that are independent and standard is attainment; the absence of it from somewhere is non-attainment. Just as the flow of water, which naturally moves downwards, is blocked by a dam, so here too, the natural capacity of the mind-stuff—which is of the nature of happiness and light—to generate discriminative realization is attainment. That does not happen because of the obstruction of merit or darkness (<term>tamas</term>). Through merit—or the practice of the limbs of Yoga—upon its removal, it attains that capacity to generate it because its nature is to have unobstructed movement. As it will say: "The cause is not the activator of the *prakṛtis* <gloss>primordial nature</gloss>, but the breaking of the cover, like a farmer."

Thus, the cause of attainment has been stated in relation to the work characterized as discriminative realization. However, it says it is also the cause of separation in relation to secondary works: **"Cause of separation."** It states the cause of distinctness: **"Cause of distinctness is like the goldsmith for gold,"** such as a bracelet, earring, or armlet, which are different or non-different from the gold. In terms of intent, when one wants to distinguish it from the bracelet, the gold is different from the earring; when one wants to see them as non-different, the bracelet and the gold are non-different. Thus, the bracelet-maker, the goldsmith, by making the earring different from the gold that is non-different, is the cause of distinctness. Although fire is also the cause of distinctness for what is cooked, one cannot say it is the cause of distinctness for the substance because the qualities of being *pulāka* <gloss>grain</gloss> and *taṇḍula* <gloss>rice</gloss> are fleeting, while the substance remains. Therefore, it is said to be only the cause of change, so there is no confusion. And one should not explain that the difference in form is the cause of the distinctness of the substance. Because of the inconsistency with the example of the goldsmith. Having provided the external cause of distinctness, it illustrates the internal one: **"Thus, in the case of one perception of a woman,"** etc. Ignorance is the knowledge that "this is a lovely young woman." Because of the union with delusion, the perception of the woman becomes...

22½. The length of a longish quadrilateral is 120 (*dandas*) and the breadth is 40. The ditch around is as big as 4 *dandas* in breadth and 3 in depth. (Find out the cubical contents.)

The rule for arriving at the value of the cubical contents of an excavation, when the depth of the excavation varies (at various points), and also for arriving, when the cubical contents of an excavation are known, at the depth of digging necessary in the case of another (known) area (so that the cubical contents may be the same) :—

23½. The sum of the depths (measured in different places) is divided by the number of places; this gives rise to the (average) depth. This multiplied by the top area (of the excavation) gives rise to the (required) cubical contents of the excavation in the case where that area is trilateral, quadrilateral or circular. The cubical contents (of a given excavation), when divided by the (known) value of another area, gives rise to the depth (to which there should be digging, so that the resulting cubical contents may be the same).

<header>CHAPTER VIII.—CALCULATIONS REGARDING EXCAVATIONS. 263</header>

22½. The length of a longish quadrilateral is 120 <term>daṇḍas</term> and the breadth is 40. The ditch around is as big as 4 <term>daṇḍas</term> in breadth and 3 in depth. Find out the cubical contents.

The rule for arriving at the value of the cubical contents of an excavation, when the depth of the excavation varies at various points, and also for arriving, when the cubical contents of an excavation are known, at the depth of digging necessary in the case of another known area so that the cubical contents may be the same:

23½. The sum of the depths measured in different places is divided by the number of places; this gives rise to the average depth. This multiplied by the top area of the excavation gives rise to the required cubical contents of the excavation in the case where that area is trilateral, quadrilateral, or circular. The cubical contents of a given excavation, when divided by the known value of another area, gives rise to the depth to which there should be digging, so that the resulting cubical contents may be the same.

->*Examples in illustration thereof.*<-

24½. In an equilateral quadrilateral field, the ground covered by which has an extent measured by 4 <term>hastas</term> in length and breadth, the excavations are in depth 1, 2, 3, and 4 <term>hastas</term> in four different cases. What is the measure of the average depth of the excavations?

25½. There is a well with an equilateral quadrilateral section, the sides whereof are 18 <term>hastas</term> in measure; its depth is 4 <term>hastas</term>. With the water of this well, another well measuring 9 <term>hastas</term> at each of the sides of the section is filled. What is the depth of this other well?

<note>For finding out the total length of the surrounding ditch when the central mass of earth is rectangular in section, the measures of the sides as increased by the width or half the width of the ditch are added together, according as the <term>Karmāntika</term> or the <term>Aundra</term> result is required.</note>

# Mānasollāsa | 167
### [Book 4]

An iron target, sixteen fingers wide and of equal height, should be made to resemble an elephant, and one should practice upon it. <note>verse 44</note>

One should firmly tie these <note>targets</note> between two branches of a pillar, at the height of a man's chest, three times over. <note>verse 45</note>

Having pierced them and passed through, and then having penetrated the ground at the end, one should shoot in such a way that the arrow remains standing properly, while being skilled in the technique. <note>verse 46</note>

When the arrow is held by the thumb and the side of the index finger, and the bow is held in the fist, with the nock properly placed, it is called <term>samasandhāna</term> <gloss>even-joining</gloss>. <note>verse 47</note>

In <term>samasandhāna</term> <gloss>even-joining</gloss>, the release from the bowstring should be from below. Therefore, joining from above is known as <term>ūrdhvasandhāna</term> <gloss>upward-joining</gloss>. <note>verse 48</note>

When the target is far above, one should use the lower joining <note>technique</note>; for a low target, one uses the upper <note>joining</note>; for an even target, the even <note>joining</note> should be used. <note>verse 49</note>

A target sixteen fingers in circumference is called a thick target. A subtle one is two fingers <note>thick</note>, with a five-finger head. <note>verse 50</note>

A target inferred by sound is called supreme and secondary. Thus, five types of targets should be demonstrated in their piercing. <note>verse 51</note>

Moving sideways, moving forward, spinning, or leaping; their locations are said to be in the sky, on the ground, or in water. <note>verse 52</note>

Two hundred <note>fingers distance</note> is said to be excellent; one hundred and fifty is medium; one hundred and twenty is the lowest distance on the ground for an archer. <note>verse 53</note>

One should strike the excellent distance slowly with four arrows, which are even-feathered, thick or thin, or featherless and nimble. <note>verse 54</note>

The King should demonstrate the lightness of hand by shooting one arrow at a falling target, one at a hand-held one, and five at one in the sky, thus executing the target practice. <note>verse 55</note>

"सप्तसु छन्दःसृचः कल्पयित्वा गायत्र्यादि 'गायत्र्यै स्वाहा' इत्येवं यथाछन्दः" (शांक १८,१) इति तत्रैव शान्तিকল্পे मन्त्राणाम् ऊहनप्रकारस्य दर्शितत्वात् 'गायत्र्यै स्वाहा', 'उष्णिहे स्वाहा', 'अनुष्टुभे स्वाहा', 'पङ्क्त्यै स्वाहा', 'त्रिष्टुभे स्वाहा', 'जगत्यै स्वाहा', इत्येवम् अस्मिन् सूक्ते सप्त मन्त्रा भवन्ति । सर्वे मन्त्राः स्पष्टार्थाः ।

**इति तृतीयेऽनुवाके प्रथमं सूक्तम् ।**

'आङ्गिरसानामाद्यैः' इत्यादिसूक्तद्वयस्य 'आङ्गिरसीं गणकामस्य अभिवरनोऽभिवर्षमाणस्य च' (शांक १७,२) इति विहितायाम् आङ्गिरस्याख्यायां महाशान्तौ विनियोगः । उक्तं हि शान्तিকল্পे— "समासः" (१९,२२:२३) आङ्गिरस्याम् । 'इन्द्र मरुत्व' (अ२,५) इत्येन्द्रयाम्" (शांक १८,१;४) इति । अत्र समासशब्देन एतत् सूक्तद्वयम् उच्यते ।

तत्र 'आङ्गिरसानामाद्यैः' इति सूक्तम् एवम् आम्नायते—

**The recitation of that hymn is:**

"To the Gayatri, to the Ushnih, to the Anushtubh, to the Brihati, to the Pankti, to the Trishtubh, to the Jagati." || 1 ||

"Having fashioned the verses into seven meters, such as the Gayatri..."—since the method of changing the mantras in the <term>Śāntikalpa</term> is shown as "To the Gayatri <term>svāhā</term>," "To the Ushnih <term>svāhā</term>," "To the Anushtubh <term>svāhā</term>," "To the Pankti <term>svāhā</term>," "To the Trishtubh <term>svāhā</term>," "To the Jagati <term>svāhā</term>," there are seven mantras in this hymn. All the mantras are clear in meaning.

**Thus ends the first hymn in the third <term>anuvāka</term>.**

The two hymns beginning with "By the first of the Angirasas" are applied in the <term>Mahāśānti</term> called "Angirasi," which is prescribed for one who desires a calculation of the Angirasas and for one who desires to obtain rain or who is experiencing rainfall. It is said in the <term>Śāntikalpa</term>: "The collection (19.22:23) in the Angirasi. 'Indra Marutvan' (2.5) in the Indri." Here, the word "collection" refers to these two hymns.

There, the hymn "By the first of the Angirasas" is recited as follows:

By the first of the Angirasas, five <term>anuvākas</term>; <term>svāhā</term>. || 1 ||

To the sixth; <term>svāhā</term>. || 2 ||

To the seventh and eighth; <term>svāhā</term>. || 3 ||

To the blue-nailed ones; <term>svāhā</term>. || 4 ||

To the green ones; <term>svāhā</term>. || 5 ||

To the small ones; <term>svāhā</term>. || 6 ||

To the sequences; <term>svāhā</term>. || 7 ||

To the first powerful ones; <term>svāhā</term>. || 8 ||

To the second powerful ones; <term>svāhā</term>. || 9 ||

To the third powerful ones; <term>svāhā</term>. || 10 ||

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of the Sefer HaBahir, focusing on the structural foundations of the world and the divine names. It follows previous discussions on the nature of the Sefirot (divine emanations).</meta>

# The Book of Illumination (Sefer HaBahir)

world. And if he were weak, he would not be able to sustain the world. Therefore, it is not the world [itself], but rather **one Righteous One** who sustains the world, as it is written: *“The Righteous One is the foundation of the world.”* <note>Proverbs 10:25. In Kabbalah, the "Zaddik" or Righteous One refers to the Sefirah of Yesod (Foundation).</note> Therefore: *“Take My offering from Me”* first, and afterward: *“And this is the offering which you shall take from them”*—from the remainder. And what is this? *“Gold,”* etc. Another interpretation: *“That they take for Me an offering”* <note>Exodus 25:2</note>—they shall take for the Holy One an offering, which is the letter **Yod** [י], and it is the tenth. And from where do we know that the tenth is holy? As it is written: *“The tenth shall be holy.”* <note>Leviticus 27:32</note> And what is this "Holy"? As it is written: *“The first of all the first-fruits of all, and every offering of all,”* etc. <note>Ezekiel 44:30</note> and it is written: *“The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord.”* <note>Psalm 111:10</note> Do not read it as "Fear of the Lord" but as "The Vision of the Lord" <note>original: *Mar'ot YHVH* instead of *Yirat YHVH*</note> (others say: *“And the fear of the Lord”*).

His students asked Rabbi Akiva: "Our teacher, what is the meaning of *'Sanctify to Me every firstborn'*? <note>Exodus 13:2</note> Is the Holy One, blessed be He, a firstborn?" He said to them: "No, *'Sanctify to Me every firstborn'* refers to the second [level] in holiness, and it is called by the name of Israel, as it is written: *'Israel is My son, My firstborn.'* <note>Exodus 4:22</note> As it were, He was with them at the time of their enslavement. And this is what is written: *'You shall surely let the mother go,'* etc. <note>Deuteronomy 22:7</note> It does not say 'You shall surely let the father go,' but rather 'You shall surely let the mother go' out of honor for those who are called 'the world,' as it is said: 'The mother is the firstborn' (and some say: 'the firstborn of firstborns'). And she is called **Atzeret** <note>The "Assembly" or the holiday of Shavuot/Shemini Atzeret</note>, who is called 'Mother,' as it is said: *'For if you call out to understanding [Binah]'* <note>Proverbs 2:3. In Kabbalah, Binah is the Divine Mother.</note>. And what is *'but the children you may take for yourself'*? Rabbi Rahumai said: Those children that she raised. And what are they? The seven days of Sukkot, which are the seven days of the week. There is a difference between them, for they are higher in holiness, as it is written regarding them: *'A holy convocation.'* And is Atzeret then a holy convocation? He said to them: Yes. But this is **A-H-V-H** <note>A divine name permutation</note> as it is written: *'On the first day a holy convocation'* and *'on the seventh day a holy convocation.'* He asked: 'Why is Atzeret alone?' Because on it the Torah was given to Israel. And when the Torah was created, it was the 'Beginning' <note>Reshit</note>; the Holy One, blessed be He, ruled His world with it alone, as it is written: *'The beginning of wisdom.'* He said: 'Since it is so, your holiness shall be for you alone.' And what is Sukkot? He said to him: A **House** [Bayit], as it is written: *'With wisdom a house is built.'* <note>Proverbs 24:3</note> And from where do we know that Sukkot is a house? As it is written: *'And Jacob journeyed to Sukkot and built for himself a house.'* <note>Genesis 33:17</note>"

### Rabbi Berechiah sat and expounded:
What is the meaning of "hanging"? It is a hint that there is before the Holy One, blessed be He, a place in which all the spheres are included, as it is written: *“His locks are wavy [taltalim].”* <note>Song of Songs 5:11. A wordplay on 'hanging' or 'mounds'.</note> And what is this sphere? It is the belly. And what is the heart? As it is written: *“unto the heart of the heavens,”* etc. Included within are the **32 wondrous paths of wisdom**. What is the meaning of that which is written: *“The Lord bless you and keep you; the Lord make His face shine upon you and be gracious to you; the Lord lift up His countenance upon you and give you peace”*? <note>The Priestly Blessing, Numbers 6:24-26</note> This is the **Explicit Name** <note>Shem HaMephorash</note> of the Holy One, blessed be He, and it is a name of twelve [letters], as it is written: *YHV"D YHV"H YHV"D*. This teaches that the names of the Holy One, blessed be He, are three armies, and each army is not like its fellow, and they are all sealed with His name in **Y-H-H**. And how does 24 combine with the name YHVH? That is one: *“The Lord bless you,”* and also the second: *“The Lord make His face shine,”* with the 24 names of the Holy One, blessed be He; and also the third: *“The Lord lift up,”* with the 24 names of the Holy One, blessed be He. And now combine the 24 and also with the 24 names of the Holy One, blessed be He—three times will be the **72 names** of the Holy One, blessed be He, which emerge from [the verses] *“And he journeyed,” “And he came,” “And he stretched out.”* <note>Exodus 14:19-21. Each verse has 72 letters, used to derive the 72-letter Name of God.</note> And who are these ministers? This teaches that there are three: for **Gevurah** (Might) is the minister of all the holy forms, and thus it is on the left side of the Holy One, blessed be He, where **Gabriel** stands. And on His right are all the holy forms, **Michael**. And in the center is the **Truth**, the minister of all the holy forms. And each minister has 24 forms, and there is no end to his legions, as it is written: *“Is there any number to His legions?”* If so, are there another 72 and 72? He said: Do not say so, except at the time when Israel offers a sacrifice before their Father in Heaven, they are unified. And this is the unity of our God. And why is it called a *Korban* [sacrifice]? Because it brings the holy powers close <note>wordplay: *Korban* (sacrifice) and *Karav* (to draw near)</note>, as it is written: *“And join them one to another into one stick,”* etc. And it says: *“for a pleasing aroma”*—and there is no aroma except in the nose, and there is no breath (which is the smelling) except in the nose. And there is no *Nichoach* [pleasing/rest] except a descent, as it is said: *“And He descended,”* which the Targum translates as *“And He rested”* [Ve-nachat]. And He descends and is unified with the holy forms, and they are brought close through the sacrifice. And this is what is written: *“A sacrifice to Him.”* <insert>(Others say: The Name that emerges from the three verses *'And he journeyed,' 'And he came,' 'And he stretched out.'* The first verse is arranged in the order of the verse; the letters of the second verse are in reverse order; and the third verse, which is *'And he stretched out,'* is in the order of the verse. Each of the verses has 72 letters. It is found that in every single name of the 72 names emerging from these three verses... there are three letters... this is the Explicit Name that emerges from it... and it is forbidden to mention these. These are the 72 names that emerge and are divided into three parts, 24 for each part. And over each part of the three parts, a high minister is over them. And over each part, he has four directions for his name: East, West, North, South. And they are divided, and for every direction there are found... 24 forms...)</insert> And all of them are sealed with *YHVH, EHYH, Shaddai, Elohim Chayim, Shaddai, High and Exalted, Inhabiting Eternity, Whose name is Holy and Exalted, YHVH.* Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.

### Rabbi Ahala’a sat and expounded:
What is the meaning of *“The Lord reigns, the Lord has reigned, the Lord shall reign forever and ever”*? This is the Explicit Name that was placed at the head to combine and to mention, as it is written: *“And they shall put My name upon the children of Israel.”* <note>Numbers 6:27</note> And it is a name of twelve [letters] within the name of the Priestly Blessing: *“The Lord bless you,”* etc., which are

<header>Eighth Gate</header>

below, for this is superior to the place of the master. For the brilliance of his tablets below is the secret of the judgment in Understanding <term>Binah</term>. Upon the world, like a righteous man in his dwelling, and in his daughter in the creation and her host, everything precedes the coming of the singular and unique one. The place is assigned to her, and the word is alone, influenced but not influencing. To grasp the light, they needed to ascend to them. And the secret of the daughter is a path of water that includes the designated time of the Kingship <term>Malchut</term>. 

The secret of the sign of the covenant <note>the Sefirah of Yesod</note> is that it is the foundation <term>Yesod</term>, for it only influences the aura of the world from the source of life. The navel is designated from the joints and the flowing waters from within the well. It was not said that they flowed from the eye, but from the foundation, which is like a curtain drawn from the source. Therefore, it said "flowing" and "subduing." Those who are sweetened by the judgments in the secular world return and repeat the light in the secrets of the hands that encompass the one who is balanced. It is wrapped in the light of the day, as it is said: "He cuts the waters by His mouth." This means the flowing waters are after the source of <term>Tiferet</term> and it is in the middle of the path. One who prepares the right side digs the pit of the soul. For Abraham to dig them, the Philistines hid them. 

The entire Chariot <note>the divine structure</note> is found to be hinted at in this, according to the secret of the Sefirot. There is here the secret of the eye that looks at the Holy One, Blessed be He, with the names of the unique ones. This refers to their roots above, for in the internal waters from the resting place, this is the secret of the descent. For God's blessing is upon the fountain in the secret of "he will see from the look." He establishes himself like an embrace of the right side, as it is written: "his right hand embraces me." This is in order to be included in the secret of the influence and the speech from above, in the secret of the upper beard that sweetens the male waters for the Kingship. In the right side is the secret for those below. Thus, these are the two righteous ones and the judgments. 

The female aspect is the answer of the roses. The image of Jacob is carved below. Although he was small, he was similar to the image on the Throne. It was like the image in the windows. Furthermore, all the righteous ones whose goodness is in Understanding <term>Binah</term> do not lose anything. Their teachings are also found there. This means they do not diminish in their goodness but are hidden for the future. If they were not sunken in goodness, they would be visible as stars in the days of the Messiah. See the book "The Language of Truth" regarding the building of David, King of Israel. 

Jacob is superior to all of them, for in that place he is called "the house" and not just "branches." There are further reasons in the wisdom of the soul to bring it together with the souls of the righteous, whether in the world of the infants or the world of the great. For in the vision of the world, all of them are the dwelling place of the Holy One, Blessed be He, in the body. As it is written in the portion of <term>Lech Lecha</term> <gloss>page 82</gloss>, all is one and there is no change of countenance. The qualities of the Torah are also present when the Holy One, Blessed be He, releases one from punishment. 

Regarding the soul that ascends above, it is a union and a meeting to receive the blessing like the upper fountain. Torah is never forgotten from the lower ones, and it is prepared for the end of time to assist. There is a reason for the countenances of the constant and the arrangement of the two breads upon the table, the bread of the Presence. For whom is it prepared? For the father at the start of the meal. The bread is for the blessing of the sustenance, fixed as three and three until one hundred. So too is the order of the offerings according to the secret of the meal as we have studied.

לֹא בְמַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁלֹּא נִטְלָה תְרוּמָתוֹ,
וְלֹא בְמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְהֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא נִפְדּוּ.
הַשׁוֹלֵחַ אֶת עֵרוּבוֹ בְיַד חֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן,
אוֹ בְיַד מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוֹדֶה בָעֵרוּב, אֵינוֹ עֵרוּב.
אִם אָמַר לְאַחֵר: קַבְּלוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ!
הֲרֵי זֶה עֵרוּב.

### מסכת עירובין פרק ג משנה ג
### ג

נְתָנוֹ בָאִילָן,
לְמַעְלָה מֵעֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים, אֵינוֹ עֵרוּב,
לְמַטָּה מֵעֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים,
הֲרֵי זֶה עֵרוּב.
נְתָנוֹ בְבוֹר,
אֲפִלּוּ עָמֹק מֵאָה אַמָּה,
הֲרֵי זֶה עֵרוּב.
נְתָנוֹ בְרֹאשׁ הַקָּנֶה אוֹ בְרֹאשׁ הַקֻּנְטָס,
כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהוּא תָלוּשׁ וְנָעוּץ,
אֲפִלּוּ גָבֹהַּ מֵאָה אַמָּה,
הֲרֵי זֶה עֵרוּב.
נְתָנוֹ בְמִגְדָּל וְנָעַל לְפָנָיו וְאָבַד הַמַּפְתֵּחַ,
הֲרֵי זֶה עֵרוּב.
רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר:
אִם אֵין יָדוּעַ שֶׁהַמַּפְתֵּחַ בִּמְקוֹמוֹ, אֵינוֹ עֵרוּב.

### מסכת עירובין פרק ג משנה ד
### ד

נִתְגַּלְגֵּל חוּץ לַתְּחוּם,
וְנָפַל עָלָיו גַּל, אוֹ נִשְׂרַף,
אוֹ תְרוּמָה וְנִטְמֵאת,

...even between graves,
because one can wall it off and eat there <note>original: "lakchutz"; refers to creating a temporary partition or being in a location (like a coffin or a separate area) that ritually separates the person from the impurity of the graves so they can eat the eruv meal</note>.

### Tractate Eruvin Chapter 3 Mishnah 2
### 2

We may establish an **eruv** <note>original: "eruv"; a symbolic meal that extends the distance one is permitted to walk on the Sabbath</note> with **demai** <note>original: "demai"; produce purchased from a common person where it is uncertain if the required tithes were separated</note>,
and with **first tithe** <note>original: "ma'aser rishon"; the ten percent of produce given to the Levites</note> from which the **priestly gift** <note>original: "terumah"; the portion of the tithe given by the Levite to the Priest</note> has been taken,
and with **second tithe** <note>original: "ma'aser sheni"; produce eaten by the owner in Jerusalem</note> or **consecrated property** <note>original: "hekdesh"; items dedicated to the Temple</note> that have been **redeemed** <note>exchanged for coins, which releases the food for common use</note>;
**Priests** may establish an eruv with **challah** <note>original: "challah"; the portion of dough given to the Priest</note> or with **priestly gifts**,
but we may **not** establish an eruv with **tevel** <note>original: "tevel"; produce from which tithes have not been taken at all</note>,
nor with **first tithe** from which the priestly gift has not been taken,
nor with **second tithe** or **consecrated property** that have not been redeemed.
One who sends his **eruv** by the hand of a **deaf-mute**, an **insane person**, or a **minor** <note>these individuals are not considered legally responsible agents in Jewish law</note>,
or by the hand of someone who does **not acknowledge** the laws of the **eruv** <note>such as a Cuthean/Samaritan, who might not treat the mission with the necessary religious care</note>,
it is not a valid **eruv**.
But if he said to another person <note>a legally responsible adult</note>: "Receive it from him!"
it is a valid **eruv**.

### Tractate Eruvin Chapter 3 Mishnah 3
### 3

If one placed the eruv in a **tree**:
If it is **above ten handbreadths** <note>original: "tefachim"; a handbreadth is about 3-4 inches. Above ten handbreadths, the eruv is technically in a different "domain," making it inaccessible</note>, it is **not** a valid **eruv**;
If it is **below ten handbreadths**,
it is a valid **eruv**.
If one placed it in a **pit**,
even if it is **one hundred cubits** <note>original: "ammah"; a cubit is about 18 inches</note> deep,
it is a valid **eruv**.
If one placed it at the **top of a reed** or at the **top of a pole**,
as long as it is **detached and stuck** in the ground <note>meaning it is no longer a growing plant but a piece of wood</note>,
even if it is **one hundred cubits** high,
it is a valid **eruv**.
If one placed it in a **tower** <note>a storage chest or cabinet</note> and **locked it**, and the **key was lost**,
it is a valid **eruv** <note>because a locksmith could technically open it without violating major Sabbath labors</note>.
**Rabbi Eliezer** says:
If it is not **known** that the key is in its place <note>accessible to the owner</note>, it is **not** a valid **eruv**.

### Tractate Eruvin Chapter 3 Mishnah 4
### 4

If it **rolled** outside the **Sabbath limit** <note>original: "techum"; the 2,000-cubit boundary around a town</note>,
or if a **heap of stones** fell on it, or if it **burned**,
or if it was a **priestly gift** and became **ritually impure**...

Behold, I have found written in books that the angel appointed over dreams is Gabriel, and he is in charge of all matters concerning dreams and everything that a person sees in his dream. Therefore, a person must be very careful not to see vain dreams and not to occupy himself with idle matters before he sleeps, so that evil thoughts do not come to him in his dream. A person also needs to recite the <term>Kriat Shema</term> <gloss>the Shema prayer recited before bed</gloss> with great intention so that the angels will guard him from every evil occurrence, every bad dream, and every evil thought. 

I also found it written that whoever wishes to know a certain matter in his dream must fast for one day, immerse himself in pure water, wear clean clothes, and pray a pure and clear prayer. He should ask of <term>Hashem Yitbarakh</term> <gloss>the Blessed Name; God</gloss> to reveal to him the thing he desires to know. Then he should go to sleep in purity and holiness, and with the help of the Blessed Name, he will see what he seeks in his dream. 

Furthermore, a person must be careful not to tell his dream to just anyone, but only to a faithful friend or to a sage who knows how to interpret dreams according to the law. This is so that the dream does not manifest for the worse, God forbid, for <term>the dream follows the mouth</term> <gloss>a Talmudic principle that a dream's fulfillment is determined by its interpretation</gloss>. Therefore, a person must be very careful with his words and thoughts. 

I also found it written that there are dreams that are from the Blessed Name, dreams that are from the <term>Satan</term> <gloss>the Accuser/Adversary</gloss>, and dreams that arise from a person's own thoughts. Therefore, a person must be wise and distinguish between one dream and another. Whoever wants to know if a dream is from the Blessed Name should check if the dream is a good thing and if it brings the person to <term>Yirat Shamayim</term> <gloss>Fear of Heaven/Awe of God</gloss> and to the service of the Blessed Name. If it is so, then it is a good dream and from the Blessed Name. If it is an evil thing or something that brings the person to a transgression or to sadness, then it is a dream from the Adversary, and a person must distance himself from it and pay it no mind at all. A person should also always pray to the Blessed Name to guard him from every bad dream and every evil thought, and merit him to see good dreams that herald good tidings for him and for all Israel. Amen and Amen.

# פרשת תולדות תורה שבכתב
## זה שמו אשר יקראו לו מקור הברכות

### נר מצוה

<margin>
ויזרע יצחק בארץ ההיא וימצא בשנה ההיא מאה שערים ויברכהו ה' אמרו בכ"ר והביא רש"י כפירושו מאה שערי' שאמדוה כמה ראויה לעשו' ועשת על אחת שאמדוה מאה וברבותינו ז"ל אמרו אומד זה למעשרות היה
</margin>

הנה האבות קיימו כל התורה והתורה פרשה מדה זו בפרטיו מצות שנוהגו כמו שמצינו באברהם אבינו ונתן מעשר מכל וכאן ביצחק וכן ביעקב שאמר וכל אשר תתן לי עשר אעשרנו לך ויעקב אבינו נתן מעשר אפילו מנפשות כמו שחז"ל שיש י"ד שבטים עם אפרים ומנשה דל' ד' ככורות לאמהותיהן שהם בעצמן קודש נשארו עשרה והופרשו לוי להיות קודש לוי הרי קיימו האבות מצות מעשר בכל לבבם ובכל נפשם ובכל מאודם מאודם כפשוטו מעשר מכל אף מעשר כספים ובכל נפשם דהיינו יעקב עישר מנפשות בניו ובכל לבבם זה שייך לתרומה גדולה שאין לה שיעור רק כפי נדבת לבו ובא תרומת ה' ואמז"ל עין יפה א' מארבעים בינוני א' מחמשים עין רעה א' מס' והכל רמוז בפסוק ויתן לו מעשר מכל והיה די שיאמר ויתן מעשר אלא מכל הוא רמוז על תרומה גדולה כי תרומת מעשר היא בכלל המעשר כמו שאפרש אח"כ כי נתן למלכי צדק המעשר וגם התרומ' מעשר והנה חז"ל עולה חמשי' שהוא עין בינוני הנותן א' מחמשים אבל אברהם חסיד עשרה מחמשים כדי ליתן מהם תרומה גדולה דבהסרת עשרה מחמשי' נשארו ארבעים כלומר נתן חלק אחד מארבע' לתרומה גדולה ונתן לו ואף שדרך בינוני א' מכ"ל דהיינו א' מחמשי' א' מכ"ל דהיינו א' מחמשי' א"כ כשלקח תרומ' כד"ל הסיר עשרה מחמשי' ואח"כ הפריש א' לתרומה גדולה כי היה נדיב לב וקוכל האבות ועל ענין תרומה גדולה נרא' לתרץ מ"ש אומד זה למעשרות וקשה הא תנן ואל תרבה לעשר אומד ות אלא יצחק אבינו היה מורר ומעשר והאומד היה בתרומ' גדול' כדתנן במסכת תרומה פ"א אין תורמין לא במרה ולא במשקל ולא במנין אע"פ שנתנו חכמים שיעור כדלעיל עין טוב' כו' מ"מ נקראת מאומד וילפינן מדכתיב ותחשב לכם תרומתכם כחשיב' אשר תור' כלומר כאומד ואף על גב דבתרומת מעשר כתיב אם אינו ענין לתרומת מעשר שהרי נתנה התור' שיעור וצריך למדוד כו' תנהו לענין תרומ' גדול'.

אמנם כי דייקת שפיר משמע דהאומד היה בשביל כל המעשרות דהא האומד הזה קודם המאמ"י שאמרו השדה כמה ראוי לעשות כו' ונרא' בודאי בשעת הפרשת המעשר היה מודד להפריש המעשר והאומד שהי' קודם צמיחת יבוא עליהם חסידות דהדין הוא שאין חייב אלא לאחר גמר מלאכ' ואחר שירא פני הבית ומה שאוכלו מתנהג בזה חסידות גמור מהמעשר ויצחק רצה להחמיר ולזה היה אומר כו' להפריש אף ממה שנאכל בכר כדי זה הכלל ואל תעשר אומדות כי זה לא נאמר רק על חיוב מעשר אבל זה היתה חומרא כדעלמא מיצחק אבינו ומאחר שזה הפסוק מדבר ממצות מעשר ע"כ אמר ויברכהו ה' וכמו שכתוב במלאכי הביאו את כל המעשר אל בית האוצר וגו' ובחנוני נא בזאת והריקותי לכם ברכה עד בלי די ומה שכתבתי שנתנו למלכי צדק התרומות והמעשרות הלא המעשרות לא שייכי' רק ללוים' דע כי מלכי צדק היה שם בן נח ובכל כח היה לוי לפי מה שקבלנו מחז"ל ול' שהאהרן הכהן הוא ממלכות מלכי צדק ע"כ מלכי צדק היה צדק עליון ושמואל הנביא שהיה לוי הוא מנשמת אהרן וזהו רמז והוצאותיו ואחיך הלוי ומלכי צדק הוא שם בן נח' ותראי דשם ישבו של שם ועבר כו' ואז חל על שלם שם ע"כ מלכי צדק כח קולו בכח נשמתו:

### תורה אור

<margin>
דע כי סוד המעשרות וסוד הברכות הכל הולך אל מקום אחד ע"ב נאמר ברכה כמעשר וסוד הענין וימצא מאה שערים גם לענין ברכות אמרו רז"ל חייב אדם לברך מאה ברכות בכל יום ענין מאה שערים כתב הרקנאטי
</margin>

וז"ל דע כי חכמי הקבלה אמרו כי הארץ העליונ' מאה שערים לכל שער בית קבול נובעת מעייני הברכה לעולם ומשם ינק יצחק אבינו ע"ה מאה מיני ברכות שמאה שערים הנזכר שם ישבו והשפע ואצילות לכל הנבראים ולפיכך נמצא באוהל מועד מאה אדנים למאת הככר ככל לארץ שאין לך ארץ שלא יהיה לו בית קבול כו' מ"ש שחני אגלה הסוד ביותר הנה סוד המעשר הוא י' ויש לה נ' עניינים א' י' בעצמה ב' קוצו של י' שהוא נקודה וכל נקודה היא י' קטנה ג' מילוי של י' היא ג"כ עשרה כזה יו"ד ו"ד עולה י' והנה האצילות הוא ט' ספירות ומה שהיא י' הוא מצד החכמ' שהשם ית"ש רמז כו' כמו שהאריך הפרדס מספר ספירות הוא מצד חכמה וז"הו וישתי' בכתר' משלים המנין וקוצה של י' רומז על הכתר כמ"ש המקובלים כי יש עשר ספירות בחכמ' ודקות נרמזים בקוצו של י' שהיא היתה נעלמת ומילוי ה"י' הוא התפשטות עשר ספירות באופן שכל אחת כלולה מעשר ו' ומדה אדנ"י שהוא סוד הארץ העליונ' מקבלת אותם והם סוד מאה אדני' הרי לך סוד מעשר מן המעשר כי באדנ"י הם מאה שערים ומתעלמים בחכמ' הכוללת עשרה בעולם' ואח"כ מתעלמי' ביותר בתכלית העלם בקוצו של י' עד שמתהדר' ומתעלמי' בהעלם מוחלטי' וע' עצמה שהיא <meta>This page continues the Kabbalistic exploration of the "One Hundred Blessings," specifically linking them to Isaac’s "hundredfold" harvest in the Torah portion of Toledot. It builds on the previous page's discussion of the hierarchical relationship between the Priest, Levite, and Israelite as reflections of levels of the soul.</meta>

# The Portion of Toledot - The Written Torah
## This is the name by which it shall be called: The Source of Blessings

### The Lamp of the Commandment

<margin>
"And Isaac sowed in that land and found in that year a hundredfold, and the Lord blessed him." <note>Genesis 26:12</note> The Midrash <note>Bereishit Rabbah</note> says, and Rashi brings in his commentary, that "a hundredfold" <note>original: *Me’ah Shearim*, literally "a hundred gates" or "a hundred measures"</note> means that they estimated how much the field was fit to produce, and it produced a hundred times more than the estimate. Our Sages of blessed memory said this estimation was for the purpose of tithes.
</margin>

Note that the Patriarchs fulfilled the entire Torah. The Torah detailed this quality in its specifics—commandments that were practiced, as we find with Abraham our Patriarch, who "gave a tithe of everything." <note>Genesis 14:20</note> We find the same here with Isaac, and likewise with Jacob, who said: "And of all that You give me, I will surely give a tenth to You." <note>Genesis 28:22</note> Jacob our Patriarch even gave a tithe from souls; our Sages explained that there were fourteen tribes counting Ephraim and Manasseh, and after subtracting the four firstborns of the matriarchs <note>who are inherently holy and belong to God</note>, ten remained, and Levi was set aside to be holy. Thus, the Patriarchs fulfilled the commandment of the tithe with all their heart, all their soul, and all their might. "Their might" is understood in its plain sense as a tithe from all their wealth, including a tithe of money. "With all their soul" refers to Jacob tithing the souls of his sons. "With all their heart" relates to the Great Offering <note>term: *Terumah Gedolah* — the portion of the harvest given to the Priest</note>, which has no fixed legal measure but depends entirely on the generosity of one's heart. Regarding this "offering of the Lord," our Sages said: a generous eye gives one-fortieth; an average eye, one-fiftieth; and a stingy eye, one-sixtieth. This is all hinted at in the verse "And he gave him a tithe of all." It would have been sufficient to say "he gave a tithe," but the phrase "of all" hints at the Great Offering, for the "tithe of the tithe" <note>given by the Levite to the Priest</note> is included within the general category of tithes, as I will explain later. For Abraham gave Melchizedek the tithe and also the Great Offering. Now, our Sages calculated that 50 is the "average eye" <note>1/50th</note>. But Abraham, being a man of kindness, took ten out of fifty so he could give the Great Offering from them; by removing ten from fifty, forty remained—meaning he gave one part out of forty for the Great Offering. Even though the average way is one out of fifty, he removed ten from fifty and then set aside one for the Great Offering because he was generous of heart, like all the Patriarchs. Regarding the Great Offering, it seems we can resolve the statement "this estimation was for tithes." A difficulty arises: does the Mishnah not rule, "Do not tithe by estimation"? Rather, Isaac our Patriarch would measure and tithe, but the estimation mentioned in the verse was specifically for the Great Offering. As we learned in the Tractate of Offerings <note>original: *Terumot*, Chapter 1</note>: "We do not give the offering by measure, nor by weight, nor by count." Even though the Sages provided a proportion <note>like the generous eye</note>, it is still legally defined as being given "by estimation." We learn this from the verse: "And your offering shall be reckoned to you," meaning it is like a reckoning or an estimation of the mind. And even though this is written regarding the *tithe of the tithe*, since it is not applicable there <note>because the Torah gave a specific measure of one-tenth for that and it must be measured</note>, apply the rule instead to the Great Offering.

However, if you examine it closely, it implies the estimation was for all tithes. For this estimation preceded the actual growth, as the Sages said: "how much the field was fit to produce." It seems certain that at the time of setting aside the tithe, he would indeed measure it. But the estimation that happened before the crop grew was an act of piety. The law is that one is only obligated to tithe after the processing is finished and the crop enters the home. Isaac’s behavior before that followed the path of complete piety. He wanted to be stringent and would set aside tithes even from what was eaten casually in the field. The rule "Do not tithe by estimation" only applies to the strict legal obligation. But this was a personal stringency of Isaac our Patriarch. And since this verse speaks of the commandment of tithing, it concludes: "And the Lord blessed him." As it is written in the prophet Malachi: "Bring all the tithes into the storehouse... and test Me now in this... if I will not pour out for you a blessing until there is no room to suffice." <note>Malachi 3:10</note> Regarding what I wrote—that they gave the offerings and tithes to Melchizedek—do tithes not belong only to the Levites? Know that Melchizedek was Shem, the son of Noah, and he possessed the power of a Levite according to our tradition. It is said that Aaron the Priest descends from the "kingdom" of Melchizedek. Therefore, Melchizedek represented the "Upper Righteousness" <note>original: *Tzedek Elyon*</note>. Samuel the Prophet, who was a Levite, came from the soul-root of Aaron. This is the hint in the phrase "your brother the Levite." Melchizedek is Shem, and you see that there sat the schools of Shem and Eber... the name "Salem" <note>the root of Jerusalem, meaning "whole"</note> rested upon him. Therefore, Melchizedek's power of voice came from the power of his soul.

### Torah Light

<margin>
Know that the secret of the tithes and the secret of the blessings all go to the same place. Regarding the tithe, the word "blessing" is used. The secret of "finding a hundredfold" also relates to the blessings; our Sages said: "A person is obligated to bless one hundred blessings every day." Regarding the matter of "one hundred gates," Recanati <note>14th-century Italian Kabbalist</note> wrote:
</margin>

And these are his words: "Know that the scholars of Kabbalah said that the Upper Land has one hundred gates. Each gate is a receptacle that flows from the springs of blessing to the world. From there, Isaac our Patriarch drew one hundred kinds of blessings." For the one hundred gates are the seat of the abundance and emanation for all created beings. Therefore, in the Tent of Meeting, there were one hundred sockets <note>term: *Adanim* — the silver bases of the Tabernacle walls</note> for the one hundred talents of silver. Every "land" has a receptacle. I will reveal the secret further: The secret of the tithe <note>original: *Ma'aser*</note> is the number ten, represented by the letter *Yod*. It has three aspects: 1) The *Yod* itself. 2) The "point of the *Yod*" which is a dot, and every dot is a small *Yod*. 3) The "filling" <note>gloss: the way the letter name is spelled out</note> of the *Yod*, which is also ten—the letters *Vav* and *Dalet* of the word *Yod* equal ten. Now, the Emanation <note>term: *Atzilut*</note> consists of nine Sefirot, and the reason it is counted as ten is from the perspective of Wisdom <note>term: *Chokhmah*</note>, as the Name of God hints... as the book *Pardes* <note>Pardes Rimonim by Moshe Cordovero</note> elaborates. The number of Sefirot is from the side of Wisdom, and it "rests in the Crown" <note>term: *Keter*</note> which completes the count. The "point of the *Yod*" hints at the Crown, as the Kabbalists say there are ten Sefirot within Wisdom, and their subtleties are hinted at in the point of the *Yod*, which was hidden. The "filling" of the *Yod* is the expansion of the ten Sefirot, such that each one is comprised of ten. And the divine attribute *Adonai* <note>The Name associated with the Earth/Kingship</note>, which is the secret of the "Upper Land," receives them. These are the secret of the one hundred sockets (*Adanim*). Here you have the secret of the "tithe of the tithe," for in the name *Adonai* there are one hundred gates. They are hidden in Wisdom, which comprises ten. Afterward, they are even more hidden in the ultimate concealment in the point of the *Yod*, until they are glorified in absolute concealment. The *Yod* itself, which is Wisdom, is "carved out" of its point, which is the Crown. This is the secret of one hundred in the expansion of the Emanation and their inclusion of one another. This is the "filling" of the *Yod*. Afterward, they are hidden in their root in Wisdom, which is the essence of the *Yod*. Afterward, they are united in absolute unity in the point of the *Yod*. This is the secret of the tithe and the "tithe of the tithe." Now, the essence of Wisdom is unified with its point, which is the Crown; both are called "Thought" <note>term: *Machshavah*</note>, as we find in many places. See the *Pardes* in the section on terms under the entry "Thought." He writes there in the name of the great Kabbalist Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: "Thought is in the Upper Crown and in Wisdom. In the Upper Crown, it is Thought, but you have no grasp of it at all. Thought precedes all. Wisdom and Understanding come later, and one cannot grasp it at all. Wisdom is also called Thought because it is only grasped through thought, where the beginning of thinking occurs. About these it is said: 'How deep are Your thoughts!' <note>Psalm 92:6</note> For through the 'reckoning' in Wisdom, one comes to think about the Upper Crown." Thus far his words. Now, contemplate the secret of the tithe and the "tithe of the tithe" (the priest's portion of the tithe) and the secret of the Great Offering. This "part" exempts the rest... and is taken by estimation. Every measure is like the hundredfold harvest, in the secret of expansion. The "tithe of the tithe" is the cleaving of the essence to the point of the *Yod*. All of this is fixed in a "measure," for the Emanation is called "Measures" <note>term: *Middot* — referring to the Sefirot as divine qualities</note> which direct all existence. In Wisdom is the root of these measures, and there is the "tithe of the tithe." But the "Great Offering" hints at the essence of the point of the *Yod* itself, which is a level above the cleaving of the essence to its point. For the cleaving of the essence to its point is the cleaving of Wisdom to the Crown, but the point itself is the aspect of the Crown alone. There lies the secret of Thought hidden from thought, through the "estimation of the mind." This is the secret of why the Great Offering is taken by estimation. According to our Sages' ruling on the verse "and it shall be reckoned to you"—meaning in thought and estimation. And even though this verse was written regarding the *tithe of the tithe*, they learned it refers to the Great Offering, where it is taken by estimation. Certainly, what is required by the Torah has a secret as to why it was written here and not in its proper place. And here I say that they hinted at the aforementioned secret: it was written regarding the tithe of the tithe, which is the upper aspect of Wisdom, also called "Thought." This thought cleaves to the power within it, which is "by estimation." Even though this thought is the power of the Great Offering and can be in the Crown—a singular treasure, one out of a hundred—it is nevertheless the aspect of "thoughts toward Thought," which is estimation and not a fixed measure, for it is the root of all measures. And even though it is the number "one" (one out of a hundred), it is a light that is not part of the count, even though it is the head of the count. Therefore, "and it shall be reckoned to you" was written near the tithe of the tithe, even though its subject is the Great Offering. All these things are wondrous.

### And already...

<margin>
For he shall prepare us in the *Tikkunim* <note>The Tikkunei Zohar</note> the secret of "Blessed" (*Barukh*), which is the Holy One, Blessed be He... every one who learns for the sake of the Holy Place...
</margin>

I said that in tithes and blessings there is one secret and one place, as Recanati wrote. To explain the inner secret of the tenth... the secret of the "hundred gates" is explained, as is the secret of "and the Lord blessed him." To explain our "ancient ones" in the "Gates of Light" <note>term: *Sha'arei Orah* — a foundational Kabbalistic text by Joseph Gikatilla</note> in the first gate: the hundred sockets in the Tabernacle are modeled after the one hundred blessings that are filled from the Great Pool <note>original: *Bereichah*, a play on *Berakhah* (blessing)</note> called *Adonai*. Therefore, a person is obligated to bless one hundred blessings every day to draw from each one of the hundreds of blessings. If one is missing, it is a blemish... and he causes a defect in the "Glory of God." This is the secret of the Priest, Levite, and Israelite, which is the secret of the Breath, Spirit, and Soul <note>original: *Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah*</note>. According to this principle, King David said in "Bless the Lord, O my soul," connecting the blessings to the soul through the secret of the three tithes.

<summary>This page explores the mystical connection between Isaac’s hundredfold harvest, the practice of tithing, and the 100 daily blessings. It uses Kabbalistic letter-symbolism (the letter Yod) and the structure of the Tabernacle's 100 sockets to explain how human actions draw divine abundance from the "Upper Land."</summary>

When the Bulgars go there to trade, they place their goods in a certain spot where they leave them, then they return and find next to them what the inhabitants wish to give in exchange; if one is satisfied, one takes it, if not, one leaves it while waiting for an increase, so that the seller and the buyer do not see each other; this is also practiced in the regions of the south, in the land of the Negroes. — The peoples of Oualsou do not enter the land of the Bulgars, because in the summer they would perish there.</foreign>

تركيبها من هذه البيوت وانا اشير الى بيان ذلك على وجه لا يبقى فيه اشكال
ان شاء الله تعالى **اعلم** انا قررنا اولا اذ كل بيت من البيوت الثلاثة المذكورة
مفاصل ومنه يبتدئ فبهذا الاعتبار يصير كل بيت كالشجرة وله اغصان واعلم
اذا تقرر ما ذكرنا ان الانغام على ثلاثة اصناف كأصناف من بحر وكل بحر من

الدوكاه كالشجرة واعلم ان نغم العراق اصله ولعمله حد ولعكس عمله اسم ونغم
الراست اصله ولعمله حد ولعكس عملها اسم ونغم الدوكاه اصله ولعمله حد ولعكس
عمله اسم فمبدا عمل نغم العراق من بيت الركن وحده الى بيت الثاني وان

<meta>This page continues the technical discussion of musical modes, specifically focusing on the relationship between primary modes—conceptualized as "trees"—and their derivative melodies, referred to as "branches" or "seas."</meta>

<margin>
Correction
</margin>

The neighboring original. We have explained the commentary on the melodies <note>original: "al-angham"</note> according to how those before us composed them. It was mentioned in some of our books on the **science of melody** <note>original: "‘ilm al-nagham"</note> that the melody of **Rast** <note>the foundational mode in this system</note> is like a tree, and the rest of the melodies are like branches in relation to it. 

We shall explain the meaning of that. There is no doubt that the melody of Rast is built from the three houses, and all melodies are composed from these houses. I will point out the explanation of this in a way that leaves no ambiguity, God willing. **Know** that we established first that each house of the three mentioned houses serves as a joint or connection from which a melody begins. In this regard, every house becomes like a tree that possesses branches. 

Know that when what we mentioned is established, melodies are of three categories, like categories of a **sea** <note>original: "bahr"; a term used here to describe a melodic range or cycle</note>. Every sea comes from an origin. The house of **Iraq** <note>a specific melodic mode</note> is an origin like a tree. The house of **Rast** is an origin like a tree. The house of **Dukah** <note>meaning "second place"</note> is like a tree. 

Know that the melody of Iraq has an origin: its performance has a limit, and the reversal of its performance has a name. The melody of Rast has an origin: its performance has a limit, and the reversal of its performance has a name. The melody of Dukah has an origin: its performance has a limit, and the reversal of its performance has a name. 

The start of the performance of the Iraq melody is from the house of the **Pillar** <note>original: "al-Rukn"</note> alone to the second house. If you reverse it from the second house to the house of the Pillar, it becomes the melody of **Busalik** <note>a specific melodic mode</note>. It is a **sea** <note>original: "bahr"</note> and an **awaz** <note>original: "awaz"; a secondary or derivative mode</note> for the Iraq mode, and it is used more frequently than its origin. 

The performance of Rast starts from the first house alone to the third house. If you reverse it from the third house to the first house, it becomes the melody of **Sikah** <note>meaning "third place"</note>. It is a sea and an awaz for the Rast mode, and it is used more frequently than its origin. 

The performance of the Dukah melody begins from the second house alone to the fourth house. If you reverse it from the fourth house to the second house, it becomes the melody of **Musta'ar** <note>meaning "borrowed"</note>. It is a sea and an awaz for the Dukah mode, and it is used more frequently than its origin. 

Just as Rast has specific seas, Iraq and Dukah also have specific seas. Just as Sikah is a sea for Rast, Busalik is a sea for Iraq, and Musta'ar is a sea for Dukah. Just as **Hijaz** <note>a major melodic mode</note> is a sea for Rast, Hijaz is also a sea for Iraq. **Zarkashi** <note>a derivative mode</note> is a sea for Dukah. Just as Rast has **Panjgah** <note>meaning "fifth place"</note>...

unto the Seal <note>of Prophets</note>, and stripping them entirely of the clothing of forms, is delayed from his time. For it only appears in the emergence of the one who is the <term>Paraclete</term> and the manifestation of his specific Sainthood. 
Even if he revealed it, it is because the Seal's Prophecy is its very essence in the most perfect way possible for the emergence of Prophecy. It was folded <margin>concluded</margin> and revealed <margin>exalted is its name</margin> in its naming. No forms remained upon it. The Truth has subtle, delicate rays that manifest in the permanence of the beauty of those Truths. 
Therefore, the <term>Paraclete</term> said: "All the prophets and the revealers of the truths of their prophets [remain]." However, some of those manifestations of Prophecy remained suspended and entrusted to his revelation <insert>unto there</insert> in the manifestations of his specific Sainthood, in consideration of what is appropriate for the preparation of the time. 
There is no doubt that the lights of the <term>Malakut</term> <gloss>the celestial realm</gloss> descend without end to those who perceive them. There is no prevention in them. The ray of Holiness spreads over prepared, detached souls. The path of Truth opens for whoever knocks on its door. This means the door of God is open. The Giver of Knowledge, who is "on the clear, highest horizon," is "not stingy with the Unseen." 
In this, meanings appear at a rank that is most hidden to one of intelligence. As the "Preserved Luminous Ones" <note>original: "al-hafaza dhat al-bariq"</note> reported. "Preserved" <note>original: "mahfuz"</note> in language comes from a root meaning "to snatch away." What is meant here is a subtle Unseen hidden from the world of the senses. 
"Extinguished lights" <note>original: "makhamid al-anwar"</note> are not fixed. They are followed by a flashing light upon the soul during the "Night of the <term>Nu'uja</term>." In language, this is the violent wind that uproots houses. What is meant here is the struggle that leads to the rejection of bodily faculties. 
This is not completed except by the blowing of the winds of "Divine Attractions" <note>original: "jadhabat"</note> from the High Source. As it was said: "Blessed is he who sends the winds as glad tidings before His mercy." The "easy" approaches in an hour from its possessor — meaning the possessor of the "Preservation" — descending and approaching the light within it, while the form of that witnessing ascends from it.

PROLÉGOMENES

<margin>Prolégomènes of Ebn-Khaldoun.</margin>

<meta>continues from previous page: ury suffers due to the gap between his lifestyle and his limited means</meta> in their later generations. Eventually, all the stipends are insufficient to cover the demands of luxury and its associated habits. Need touches them, and their kings demand that they restrict their expenditures to raids and wars. They find no way to escape this, so the kings impose punishments upon them and seize what is in their hands. They reserve these resources for themselves, or they bestow them upon their children and the clients of their state. Consequently, the people become too weak to maintain their own affairs, and the ruler of the state becomes weak as they weaken.

Furthermore, when luxury increases within the state and the stipends provided to the troops fall short of their needs and expenses, the ruler of the state, who is the Sultan, finds it necessary to increase their stipends to remedy their defects and remove their grievances. However, the amount of tax collection is fixed; it neither increases nor decreases. Even if it is increased through the introduction of new levies, the amount remains limited after that increase. When the total tax collection is distributed among the stipends, and an increase has occurred for every individual due to the escalation of their luxury and the abundance of their expenses, the number of the garrison necessarily decreases compared to what it was before the stipends were increased. Then, luxury grows, and the amounts of the stipends increase further for that reason, so the number of the garrison decreases a third and fourth time. This continues until the army returns to the smallest possible numbers. The garrison weakens as a result, the strength of the state falls, and neighboring states or the tribal groups <note>original: "العصايب" (asabiyyat/tribal factions)</note> and rebels under its control grow bold against it. God then permits the extinction that He has decreed for His creation.

Moreover, luxury is corrupting to character through what it produces.

<note>Footnote 1: Manuscript A and B read: العصبيات (tribal factions).</note>

translation: and the <term>‘awḍah</term> <gloss>the remedy</gloss> [is] below it, or it is not [positioned] at the bottom. Likewise, the hand, the palm, and others are hung; the <term>‘awḍah</term> always hangs downward. This is his statement, and he says: The wound sometimes occurs where it forces you to complete amputation. As for the organ, if the wound in it is a cutting [that results in loss], it needs things that grow meat. It is not enough to only dry and prevent [swelling], but rather the drying and preventing [agent] may, from one perspective, irritate the material from which it grows. The depth and the loss in the bone may be such that it is not possible to grow completely, so a depth remains, as is the case that may happen where it grows more than is necessary, so it becomes excessive flesh. The patient who is intended to grow flesh in a wound must be moderate. Without this, the good [can turn into] excess. The growth [agent] may be such that it is possible for the meat to grow. As for the skin, it is because if it has been cut off entirely, rather, solid flesh grows in its place; hair and veins do not grow upon it. It only produces branches and grows like the meat. Among the wounds are wounds of danger: wounds that occur in the nerves and the arm, and we will mention it in the chapter on nerves. Often, hateful, bad symptoms follow it; the worst that follows a wound of the arm's extremity is discoloration, the cessation of the pulse afterward, [the arm] becoming thin, and a tendency toward fading, and the loss of strength. Spasm may follow it. Likewise, that which occurs in front of the knee at the kneecap, for bad symptoms follow it, and it is a leader [that is] rarely parted from. If a spasm occurs from such arm wounds and the treatment does not heal [it], then the treatment is the amputation of the arm.

Elnabati: Frequent in the mountains near Mecca, with flowers ranging from white to yellow, and edible, clustered fruits. It is also found in Spain. The wood is called balsamic wood. Those who say this tree lacks fruit are mistaken. — Sprengel, History of Botany, p. 257. <term>Amyris Opobalsamum</term>. Forsskål, Flora Aegyptiaco-Arabica, p. 79. Abdallatif, p. 93, 94.

Elgafeki: A small, multi-stemmed plant that spreads over rocks; with leaves coated in a viscous, honey-like juice; very small white flowers; and small, bitter, astringent seeds. — <term>Galium viscosum</term> <gloss>sticky cleavers</gloss> or <term>Aparine</term>?

29, 3—7. According to Ja‘qūbī (Houtsma, 145 top) in Klamroth, ZDMG Vol. 41 p. 422: "about natural beings, about what is found in bodies and connected with them, about that which is not found in bodies and is also not connected with them" and Uṣaibi‘a (Müller, I, p. 57) in the same place (op. cit. note 4), where the supposedly Socratic saying is cited: "Search for three ways, i.e., for the science of bodies, for the science of the incorporeal, and the science of what is indeed incorporeal but is in connection with bodies" — one should read 29, 6 instead of "separated and not connected," "not separated and (better "but") connected"; 29, 10 instead of "are not," "are"; 29, 12 instead of "is not," "is."

Cf. ibn Gabirol, Baeumker op. cit., p. 70, 3—5: "and just as the soul is discrete by itself from the body and is joined to it, yet not adhering." Palqera (Munk p. <unclear>lb</unclear> lines 4—5. Cf. 36, 4—5).

<center>And just as the soul is separate in its essence from the body and is joined to it without adhering to it.</center>

30, 11—14. Ja‘qūbī (Houtsma p. 149) in Klamroth, op. cit. p. 429: be it in the air or on (the surface of) the earth or in its interior, and the phenomena occurring therein: such as clouds, mist, thunder, lightning, wind, snow, rain, and others.

30, 15—17. Ja‘qūbī (Houtsma p. 148) in Klamroth, op. cit. p. 428: Therein — in the <term>φυσικὴ ἀκρόασις</term> <gloss>Physics (lit. natural audition)</gloss> — he treats the five things that comprise all natural beings, and without which no natural being has existence, namely matter, form, place, movement, and time. Iḫwān al-ṣafā (Dieterici p. 24 lines 3—4). See Introduction XXV.

31, 3: "Time indeed is the number of motion" = Iḫwān al-ṣafā:

<center>And it has been said that it is the number of the motions of the heavens</center>

(Dieterici, p. 35 line 6) and al-Fārābī:

<center>Time is only the number of the motion of the heavens</center>

(Dieterici *Alfarabi's philosophical treatises*. Leiden 1890 p. 23 line 6). Cf. ༄༅། །རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་རྒྱལ་པོ་དཔལ་གསང་བ་འདུས་པའི་རྒྱུད་ལས་བྱུང་བའི་དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་ཆོ་ག་ནི་འདི་ལྟ་སྟེ། དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་ཐིག་གདབ་པ་དང་། དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་ཚོན་དགབ་པ་དང་། དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་སྟེགས་བུ་བཅའ་བ་དང་། དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་མེ་ཏོག་གི་ཕྲེང་བ་དང་། དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་བུམ་པ་བཅའ་བ་དང་། དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་སྟེགས་བུ་ལ་སོགས་པ་རྣམས་ནི་དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་ཆོ་ག་ཡིན་ནོ། །དེ་ནས་དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་ཆོ་ག་ནི་འདི་ལྟ་སྟེ། དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་ཐིག་གདབ་པ་དང་། དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་ཚོན་དགབ་པ་དང་། དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་སྟེགས་བུ་བཅའ་བ་དང་། དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་མེ་ཏོག་གི་ཕྲེང་བ་དང་། དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་བུམ་པ་བཅའ་བ་དང་། དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་སྟེགས་བུ་ལ་སོགས་པ་རྣམས་ནི་དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་ཆོ་ག་ཡིན་ནོ། །དེ་ནས་དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་ཆོ་ག་ནི་འདི་ལྟ་སྟེ། དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་ཐིག་གདབ་པ་དང་། དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་ཚོན་དགབ་པ་དང་། དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་སྟེགས་བུ་བཅའ་བ་དང་། དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་མེ་ཏོག་གི་ཕྲེང་བ་དང་། དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་བུམ་པ་བཅའ་བ་དང་། དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་སྟེགས་བུ་ལ་སོགས་པ་རྣམས་ནི་དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་ཆོ་ག་ཡིན་ནོ། །དེ་ནས་དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་ཆོ་ག་ནི་འདི་ལྟ་སྟེ། དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་ཐིག་གདབ་པ་དང་། དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་ཚོན་དགབ་པ་དང་། དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་སྟེགས་བུ་བཅའ་བ་དང་། དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་མེ་ཏོག་གི་ཕྲེང་བ་དང་། དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་བུམ་པ་བཅའ་བ་དང་། དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་སྟེགས་བུ་ལ་སོགས་པ་རྣམས་ནི་དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་ཆོ་ག་ཡིན་ནོ། །

<vocab>རྒྱུད་ (Tantra), གསང་བ་འདུས་པ་ (Guhyasamaja), དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་ (Mandala), ཆོ་ག་ (Ritual/Ceremony), ཐིག་ (Line/Measurement), ཚོན་ (Color/Pigment), བུམ་པ་ (Vase/Bumpa)</vocab>
translation:
The ritual <term>choga</term> <gloss>ceremonial procedure</gloss> of the mandala arising from the king of tantras, the glorious <term>Guhyasamaja</term> <gloss>Secret Assembly</gloss>, is as follows: drawing the lines of the mandala, applying the colors of the mandala, establishing the base/platform of the mandala, the flower garlands of the mandala, preparing the vase of the mandala, and the base of the mandala, and so forth, are the rituals of the mandala. Next, the ritual of the mandala is as follows: drawing the lines of the mandala, applying the colors of the mandala, establishing the base of the mandala, the flower garlands of the mandala, preparing the vase of the mandala, and the base of the mandala, and so forth, are the rituals of the mandala.

<summary>An enumeration of the essential procedural steps required for constructing and performing the rituals of the Guhyasamaja mandala.</summary>
<keywords>Guhyasamaja, Tantra, mandala, ritual, vase, color, line measurement</keywords>

translation:
<margin>May the teachings be illuminated.</margin>

<meta>continues from previous page</meta> Through this virtue that I have cultivated in this way, may I attain the state of all-knowing <note>omniscient Buddhahood</note> through this engagement with the wisdom of the Victorious One. Furthermore, the eleven and seventeen <term>sutras</term> <gloss>discourses of the Buddha</gloss> of the Great Vehicle are to be grasped by the method of the wisdom of the teachings established by the Thus-Gone One <note>a title for the Buddha</note> in order to purify the obscurations of all beings. 

As for the overcoming power of how one knows, it is considered that there is no contradiction with others who are obscured by conceptual elaboration and the like. It is the Thus-Gone One's wisdom of victory, the emptiness that obscures the faults of sentient beings' defilements, just as gold is covered by impurities. Just as the power of my own authority, the authority of the authority of the authority does not clarify others who are gathered for the sake of amending garments, so too is the wisdom of liberation from the teachings of the Thus-Gone One, which is the wisdom of conceptual elaboration and correction, the same as the clarity of that wisdom which belongs to the minds of my own <term>sutras</term> <gloss>discourses</gloss> and <term>tantras</term> <gloss>esoteric scriptures</gloss>.

<summary>This page concludes an invocation focused on the attainment of omniscient wisdom through the purification of defilements, likening the process to refining gold and aligning the practitioner with the wisdom of the Buddha.</summary>
<keywords>Omniscience, Sutras, Tantras, Emptiness, Purification, Wisdom of the Thus-Gone One</keywords>

translation: ...because existence is absent, one will not delight in it. In this way, the monk who is a protector of nirvana has no grasping, and there is no rebirth. Having overcome the demon, having won the battle, and having completely surpassed all existence, this is the end of suffering. The monk who has cut off entities, is near-peaceful, and has a peaceful mind, that one will have no rebirth. They have completely abandoned the cycle of birth. The monk who has cut off entities, is near-peaceful, and has a peaceful mind, that one is freed from the bonds of the demon. They have completely abandoned the cycle of birth. The monk who has cut off entities and has a mind without outflows, that one has no rebirth. They have completely abandoned the cycle of birth. The monk who has cut off entities and has a mind without outflows, that one is freed from the bonds of the demon. They have completely abandoned the cycle of birth. The monk who has cut off entities and has cut off the craving for existence, that one will have no rebirth. They have completely abandoned the cycle of birth. The monk who has cut off entities and has cut off the craving for existence, that one is freed from the bonds of the demon. They have completely abandoned the cycle of birth. Whoever has well-crossed the mud, has shaken off the thorns of the village, and is the monk who tames, that is the one who is on the other shore and not on this shore. Like a snake shedding its old skin, like medicine for poison given by a snake, the monk who tames the arising anger is the one who is on the other shore and not on this shore. ...and so on, he gave permission and remained. Then, he explained the prayer made by the gatekeeper of the emptiness towards the upper direction. The teachings that remained between the abandonment and the keeping of the remnants were made clear. The emptiness that is clear and fills the entirety of the upper direction manifested as an emanation. He entered into the power of the destruction of the three gatherings and remained, having performed the great emptiness. 

Then, on the twelfth day, a good day of the Fire-Horse year, he relied on the armor of constructing the auspicious reliquary stupa. Having completed the work according to the beautiful writing, he met with the elder scholar to establish the seat and remained. Regarding the Lord himself, the clarity of the visualization was the white <term>Tara</term> <gloss>deity of compassion and longevity</gloss>. Because of the purpose of granting the empowerment of the Thus-Gone Ones, the work was not left incomplete. At the very summit of the victory of the upper government of the royal state, he held the mind of the Dharma King of Compassion, having attained the power of speech. He remained for a long time, turning the wheel of Dharma without interruption. The state equivalent to the <term>Tushita</term> <gloss>Heaven of Joy</gloss> Dharma gate, where the supreme teacher Maitreya resides, was shown clearly as the place to which he went and resided. Then, the place of the assembly of the golden-colored deities of the Lama of this place, the Lord of Dharma, was [established].
